title: Colorado rallies late, blocks Georgia Tech’s would-be winning FG to open Deion Sanders’ fourth year
content:
ATLANTA — For 58 minutes on Thursday, Colorado’s offense and special teams appeared to be letting a dominant defensive performance go for naught.

But oh, how quickly the first game of Deion Sanders’ fourth season flipped.

Colorado quarterback Julian Lewis, in his third career start, guided the Buffaloes 75 yards in 63 seconds, throwing a go-ahead 20-yard touchdown pass to Charlie Williams with 37 seconds to play. Then, defensive back Boo Carter blocked a Georgia Tech field goal attempt as time expired, preserving a 14-13 Colorado win inside Bobby Dodd Stadium.

The Buffaloes got revenge for a loss to the Yellow Jackets in last season’s season opener, and can now embrace the positives of their season opener despite a few worries.

Sanders overhauled Colorado’s roster by bringing in more than 40 new transfers this offseason. He changed the coaching staff, too, hiring new play callers on offense and defense after a disappointing 3-9 season in 2025.

The first impression of Sanders’ fourth Buffaloes team was a mixed one: a stingy defense, but an offense that couldn’t get anything going for most of the game, and a special teams unit that made too many mistakes.

The Buffaloes held the Yellow Jackets without an offensive touchdown for the game. They bottled up Georgia Tech’s two big offensive transfers, former Indiana quarterback Alberto Mendoza (17-of-23, 237 yards) and former Michigan running back Justice Haynes (64 yards on 19 carries).

But Colorado quarterback Julian Lewis struggled mightily most of the game. He had just 64 yards passing when he took the field with 1:40 left in the fourth quarter, trailing 13-7. He then completed 4-of-6 passes on that final drive for 60 yards.

The Buffaloes’ only touchdown for most of the game was a run by Micah Welch to take a 7-0 lead in the second quarter. That score was matched immediately by an 100-yard kick return by Georgia Tech’s Rahkeem Smith. The Yellow Jackets kicked a field goal late in the first half to take a 10-7 lead, and added one more late in the fourth quarter to go up 13-7 — after Colorado had a 38-yard attempt for the tie blocked.

After falling behind 14-13 with 37 seconds left, Georgia Tech drove all the way to the Colorado 27-yard line. But Aidan Birr, a finalist for the Lou Groza Award last season, had his game-winning 45-yard attempt blocked.

Our takeaways from a sloppy game and a wild finish:

It was fitting that Carter came off the edge and blocked Georgia Tech’s field goal attempt to seal the Buffaloes’ win, because Colorado won this game because of its defense.

A lot of attention will be placed on Lewis’ game-winning drive. But he would not have been in position to win the game without a defense that made stop after stop.

Colorado displayed the toughness it lacked defensively last season, looking much improved. Colorado ranked 112th in scoring defense last season, allowing 30.5 points per game, and 118th in yards per play allowed (6.14).

On Thursday, the Buffaloes held Georgia Tech to 51 rushing yards. They gave up 320 yards on the ground to the Yellow Jackets last season. They didn’t surrender an offensive touchdown for the first time since 2024.

The transfer additions sparked the win. Carter is a Tennessee transfer. Monmouth defensive line transfer Lamont Lester Jr. notched three sacks. Vanderbilt defensive back transfer Randon Fontenette and Texas linebacker transfer Liona Lefau led the team with eight tackles apiece.

Colorado changed its transfer portal approach this past offseason. It went for more proven production instead of taking fliers on former blue-chip prospects who didn’t play much at Power 4 schools. That experience proved vital on Thursday night — we’ll see how much it helps over the course of the season. — Antonio Morales

Alberto Mendoza approached his starting debut with a nod to how he would be viewed, but an effort at separation from his brother — Las Vegas Raiders quarterback and reigning Heisman Trophy winner Fernando Mendoza.

“I mean, he’s, he’s Fernando Mendoza. I’m Alberto Mendoza. We’re two different people, and what he’s done is totally separate from what I’m going to do, and what’s expected to be,” he said this spring. “I mean, I’m coming in here as Alberto Mendoza.”

And Alberto Mendoza on Thursday night looked like a quarterback with promise.

Mendoza’s numbers weren’t eye-popping, but he was accurate, efficient and made key throws, especially down the stretch. His 42-yard connection with Dalen Penson over the middle of the field in the final minute set up Georgia Tech for the potential win.

On the drive before that, which ended in a field goal, he completed a 22-yarder down the right side to Jordan Allen and a 16-yarder to Kevin Roche Jr.

Mendoza wasn’t helped by his blocking: Georgia Tech’s offensive line had a rough night, giving up three sacks, forcing Mendoza to scramble other times, and not getting much push for Haynes and the running game.

But while Georgia Tech clearly has a lot of work to do on offense, Mendoza gave reasons to feel optimistic. — Seth Emerson
